paragraphs: Rav Yitzchak son of Rav Mesharsheya.

Hyman places him in Rav Papa’s time. In [Avodah Zarah 8b](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.8b.3) the Gemara challenges R’ Papa: “But Rav Yitzchak son of Rav Mesharshiya visited!” It answers that R’ Yitzchak son of R’ Mesharshiya is different, being a distinguished person. Hyman cites [Sheiltot, Kedoshim 101](https://www.sefaria.org/Sheiltot_d'Rav_Achai_Gaon.101.3) in connection with [Kiddushin 32b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.32b.3) and places him at the wedding of Abba Mar, described here as Rav Papa’s grandson [בריה דריה]. R’ Papa raised a cup to him; he did not rise before him, and R’ Papa took offense. In [Chullin 104b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.104b.12-13) he visited Rav Ashi’s house. They brought him cheese and he ate it; they brought him meat and he ate it without washing his hands. He said to him, “But Agra taught…” He said to them, “That applies at night,” etc.

He is also mentioned in [Eruvin 32b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.32b.10), [Avodah Zarah 14a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.14a.11), [Avodah Zarah 15a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.15a.8), [Menachot 24b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.24b.15) (and Rav Ashi resolves his difficulty).[^4]

notes.text: Agra is named as a reciter in the checked passage; it is not “reward.” The unusual supplied בריה דריה is understood as grandson, but the precise Kiddushin reading remains a source question.

No new primary scalar was returned. Earlier Chullin evidence about Agra the reciter and at NIGHT is inherited, not freshly inspected or reward/mush. The unusual supplied בריה דריה is retained beside contextual grandson; no SheiltotKedoshim witness or admitted family relationship was obtained. The compressed Chullin objection is singular He said to him, followed by He said to THEM; speakers remain unspecified rather than inventing a plural questioning party. All explicit full רב titles in the heading, first quoted full YitzchakMesharshiya, Papa and Ashi remain Rav. In the separate compressed ר״פ and ר״י/ר״מ occurrences the connected names are contextual readings and their titles remain R-prime. Hyman’s chronology, wedding attribution and RavAshi resolving his difficulty remain attributed reports, not new identity or dating proof.

Avodah Zarah 8b names Yitzchak son of Mesharshya and describes his withdrawal from a feast, explaining that he was a distinguished guest. Kiddushin 32b in the consulted Bavli calls the wedding guest Yitzchak son of Yehudah. Sheiltot, Kedoshim 101, calls him Yitzchak son of Mesharshya. Both consulted wedding accounts describe Abba Mar as Rav Papa’s son. Hyman’s notice here has בריה דריה, rendered contextually as grandson. In a separate discussion (vol. II, p. 793), Hyman likewise describes Abba Mar as Papa’s son and argues for the Sheiltot’s reading of the guest’s name. In the consulted Chullin 104b, those present ask their question in the plural; Hyman’s abridged account has a singular question. Both give a plural reply and distinguish night. The Bavli names the reciter Agra as Rabbi Abba’s father-in-law. Menachot 24b names Yitzchak in the objection and gives Rav Ashi’s response immediately after it.

Kiddushin names Yitzchak son of Yehudah at the wedding; the Sheiltot names Yitzchak son of Mesharshya. Both call Abba Mar Rav Papa’s son. Hyman’s supplied wording has an additional generation. Heilprin’s notice cites the Eruvin, Menachot, Chullin and Avodah Zarah occurrences. See [Heilprin’s corresponding entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2209&lang=en).
